newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy car incentives should not end abruptly-min.
newsitem.headline: Italy car incentives should not end abruptly-min.

text.p: An Italian car incentives scheme which has led to a sharp recovery in registrations over the past six months should not be terminated abruptly, Transport Minister Claudio Burlando said on Wednesday.
Burlando was speaking to ANFIA, the Italian car makers' association.
Referring to the car incentives -- which were introduced in January -- Burlando said the government wanted "to avoid abrupt downscaling."
Fiat chairman Cesare Romiti has warned against the dangers to the car industry of a sudden end to the incentives.
Under the scheme, Italians can obtain discounts if they trade in cars which have been on the roads for more than 10 years for new ones. Milan newsroom +392-66102321
